html:
The last and most destructive war between the Roman and Persian empires, fought from 602 to 628. It is sometimes called the last great war of antiquity.

When the usurper Phocas murdered Emperor Maurice in 602, the Persian shah Khosrow II, whom Maurice had put on his throne, declared war to avenge him. Persian armies took Mesopotamia, Syria and Palestine. In 614 they took Jerusalem and carried off the relic of the True Cross, and by 621 they held Egypt. In 626 Persians and Avars besieged Constantinople itself.

Heraclius, who had overthrown Phocas in 610, struck back by going on the attack deep into Persia, with help from Turkic allies. He won at Nineveh in 627, and Khosrow was overthrown and killed by his own son in 628. Persia gave back all it had taken. But both empires were drained of men and money, and within a decade the Arab conquests took Syria and Egypt from Rome at the Yarmuk and destroyed the Sasanian Empire.
sum: The last and most destructive war between the Roman and Persian empires, fought from 602 to 628. It is sometimes called the last great war of antiquity.
